title: How To CRUSH The Scandinavian Defense | The Sensei Speedrun | Grandmaster Naroditsky

moves.spoken: We take White and Black answers with the Scandinavian.
We take the pawn on d5.
We develop the knight to c3, hitting the queen with tempo.
Black retreats the queen all the way to d8 — the modern, solid setup that's gained popularity. The clean way to meet it is straightforward: occupy the centre, then develop naturally and actively.
We begin by seizing the centre with d4.
Black plays c6; we develop the knight to f3.
Black plays h6 — already a mistake, a completely unnecessary move, and we can punish it simply by playing principled chess.
We develop the bishop to c4, aiming at f7.
Black plays the bishop to f5 — flirting with disaster, because it's ...Bf5 without the supporting ...e6.
We plant the knight on e5, aiming at f7.

Black defends with e6. Now the idea: the queen to f3 would add a second attacker on f7, and the tactic to watch for is knight-takes-f7 — if the king recaptures, the e6-pawn is pinned to it, so the queen would take on f5 and win a piece with Black's king in shambles. The bishop on c4 is perfectly safe and can always drop back to b3, and the queen can retreat if needed. It's a pattern worth filing away — the knight-f7 then queen-f5 motif recurs across many openings. Then the plan is to castle and pile a rook on the e-file to smash through on e6.
Black's better path was ...Bg4, stopping the knight from reaching e5 — and as a rule ...Bc4 should be met with ...e6 to blunt the bishop.
When Black is this far behind in development, a slow move like ...h6 is a waste he simply cannot afford.

A word on why the immediate queen to f3 is dubious: Black could grab on d4, and after the queen recaptures White has two roads — the slow bishop to f4, keeping the tension, or the tactical knight-takes-f7. But the tactical line must reckon with ...Nd7, since the c4-bishop is only singly defended and White's grip can wobble.

Even winning the exchange with knight-takes-f7, White would have to beware the knight getting trapped after ...g5 and ...Bg7 — so quietly castling is the mature approach, keeping the tactic in reserve.
We castle — the disciplined choice — with the whole attacking plan still held back for the right moment.
